Reconstructed the root automorphism action on the mixed Cartesian product of complete graphs: a rooted automorphism permutes coordinate cliques only among equal q and permutes their nonzero symbols, so orbits are the (k_q) profiles. With root initial singleton color and all others common, round t leaves one entire shell weight t and one farther region, while all weights <t are already split into profiles. The key nonstandard induction counts k_q predecessors of profile k-e_q and recovers (k-1)k from the signed count-weighted sum for k>=2; at weight one, the within-shell neighbor count q-2 distinguishes factor sizes. The terminal shell contains one orbit, giving least stable round d-1 when all q equal, else d. Derive class counts by generating polynomial product_q(1+...+z^d_q), sizes by binomial multinomial. Independent full-graph 1-WL partition reconstruction passed six mixed/equal products; examined both provided exact verifier implementations at source blob paths.
